selected_primary_idea.title: Stereochemical Closure, Not a Preferred Hand: A Tiered Test of Chirality's Functional Necessity for Chemical Life
selected_primary_idea.summary: Model stereochemical compatibility as a conditional network property and compare homochiral, cross-chiral, mixed, and explicitly unsupported alternative architectures against preregistered heredity and functional criteria.
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Source-bound evidence records and non-operational conceptual models, not living systems or molecular syntheses.
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: A compatible stereochemical closure is functionally necessary for the specified class of chiral polymer-based chemical-life architectures, while a preferred terrestrial sign and universal necessity remain unproven.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Template extension, folding, recognition, and selection interact with the stereochemical relation among participants; missing compatibility produces error, inhibition, or loss of reproducible function.
falsification_conditions: No source-supported association remains after evidence-quality sensitivity analysis.
A well-supported mixed or achiral alternative meets the declared capability criteria without closure.
The definition-sensitive codebook has unacceptable reviewer agreement.
Cross-chiral evidence invalidates the closure concept rather than merely a shared-handedness rule.

rejected_ideas.title: All life must use terrestrial handedness
rejected_ideas.reason: Conflates a contingent terrestrial convention with a universal physical law.
